:::{#def-risk}
#### Risk (expected loss)

For a random variable $Y$
and a [prediction](#def-prediction) $\hy$
(a constant, or a function $g(X)$ of a random input $X$),
the **risk** is the [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) of the
[loss](#def-loss-function)
[@wikipedia_risk_function]:

$$R \eqdef \E{L(Y, \hy)}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-risk}
#### Risk of a constant prediction

Let $Y$ be a random variable with $\P(Y = 0) = 0.5$ and $\P(Y = 2) = 0.5$,
and use the constant [prediction](#def-prediction) $\hy = 0$.
The [risk](#def-risk) under [squared error loss](#def-squared-error-loss) is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\sqf{Y - 0}}
&= 0.5 \cd \sqf{0 - 0} + 0.5 \cd \sqf{2 - 0} \\
&= 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The risk under [absolute error loss](#def-absolute-error-loss) is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\abs{Y - 0}}
&= 0.5 \cd \abs{0 - 0} + 0.5 \cd \abs{2 - 0} \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {#rem-risk-quality}
#### Risk measures the quality of a prediction

The quality of a prediction is evaluated using a [loss function](#def-loss-function)
and its expected value, the [risk](#def-risk).

:::
